errors.not_implemented: The hub declares {operation} in the contract but does not implement it yet.
errors.connection: Could not reach the hub. Check the connection and try again.

login.title: Sign in
login.setup_unknown: Could not ask this hub whether it still needs first-run setup. Sign in, or reload the page.

setup.title: Create the owner account
setup.intro: This hub has no owner yet. Create the owner account here.
setup.open_title: Setup is open to whoever opens this page first — finish it now
setup.open_body: Until the owner exists, anyone who reaches this hub can create it, so do it now. If someone else got there first, restart the hub with COREHUB_RESET_OWNER=1 and set it up again.
setup.closed_title: Setup now needs the setup token
setup.closed_body: The time in which setup was open to anyone has ended, or this hub is set to token only. Paste the token the hub wrote when it started. Restarting the hub opens setup again for a while, with no token, unless it is token only.
setup.where_title: Where to find the setup token
setup.where_body: The hub printed it once in its log when it started, and wrote it to setup-token.txt inside the data directory. On the reference stack:
setup.where_local: Running the hub outside Docker: the file is in your DATA_DIR (./data/setup-token.txt by default). A new token is generated on every restart until this account exists.
setup.token_hint: Paste it exactly; it is compared as a whole and never stored in the browser.
setup.username_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore — 2 to 40 characters.
setup.workspace_hint: The name of the first profile; "Default" when left empty.
setup.password_hint: {min} characters or more. It is never shown, logged or stored anywhere but as a hash.
setup.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
setup.submit: Create the account and sign in
setup.unattended: An unattended install can still set HUB_ADMIN_PASSWORD before the first boot; the hub then creates the owner itself and this screen never appears.

shell.segment_later: {name} arrives with its module in a later phase.
shell.no_profile_body: Your account has not been given a profile, so there is nothing to open yet. Ask an admin to give you one, then check again.

pane.resize: Resize the side pane (arrow keys resize, Home collapses, End expands)

sessions.empty: No sessions in this profile yet. Start one with New chat.
sessions.reorder: Reorder {title} (Space to pick up, arrows to move)
sessions.confirm_delete_body: Its messages go with it, and there is no undo.
sessions.retitle_hint: Let the hub name this chat again, from its own first turn.

new_chat.pick_agent: Pick the agent this chat talks to. The list is the hub's registry.
new_chat.no_agents: No agent is enabled on this hub. Install or enable one on the Agents page.
new_chat.lede: Pick an installed agent from the chips, choose a working folder if you like, then type.
new_chat.in_profile: New chat in {name}. To start it in another profile, switch the profile at the top of the page.
new_chat.none_installed: No agent is installed on this hub yet. Hermes ships with it; if it reads "not installed", check that it is running, or install one from the catalog in

chat.pick_one: Pick a session from the list, or start a new chat.
chat.empty: No messages yet. Say something below.
chat.resynced: Reconnected; the transcript was reloaded from the hub.
chat.no_provider: No model provider is configured for this profile, so the agent has nothing to run on.
chat.no_key: The provider rejected the stored key, so the agent could not reach it.
chat.pick_one_body: Every chat keeps its own agent, its folder and its history.
chat.fork_explains: Another agent copies this conversation into a new chat with it and leaves this one as it is. The model selector below changes only this chat.
chat.speak_later: Speech arrives in a later phase.
chat.anchor_missing: The message this search pointed to is no longer in this conversation.

composer.label: Message composer
composer.placeholder: Message the agent… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
composer.busy_hint: A run is active; your next message is queued behind it.
composer.drop_hint: Or drop files straight onto the composer.
composer.approval_unsupported: This agent declares no approval mode.
composer.dictate_unavailable: Dictation arrives with a speech provider (models.transcribe is still 501).

approval_hint.ask: Asks before a command or a write outside the working folder.
approval_hint.always: Asks before everything, reads included — slowest, safest.
approval_hint.auto_safe: Runs what it judges safe, asks about the rest.
approval_hint.auto_all: Runs everything without asking; nothing to object to.
approval_hint.off: No gate at all: commands, files and network without permission.

approval.answer_hint: Type your answer… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)

pending.title: Waiting for you
pending.none_body: Approvals, questions from agents and workflow steps that need you show here.
pending.pairing: {name} wants to message the agent on {platform}
pending.pairing_hint: Approve or deny the sender on the agent's channels page.

global_agent.intro: One standing conversation with your agent in this profile, outside the chats list. Reach it from search and from the bar of things waiting for you.
global_agent.no_agent: No agent is installed in this profile yet, so there is no one to talk to.

agents.limited: This agent runs through the process harness and is limited.
agents.auto_update_hint: Takes a new version as soon as it ships, without asking.

tools.not_supervised: This hub does not run Hermes itself, so it cannot ask Hermes to do this.
tools.profile_absent: Hermes has no profile named {profile} yet, so it has no files to show here.
tools.runtime_absent: Hermes is not installed or running here, so it has no folder to read.

agents.not_found: No agent with this id in this profile.

settings.global_note: This screen is hub-wide, outside the current profile.
settings.management_hint: Configured once: whole pages, not tabs.

about.agent_manager: Install, update and configure each agent
about.device_connections: Pair a phone and trusted devices

account.password_hint: This device stays signed in; your other devices are signed out.
account.password_mismatch: Does not match the new one
account.password_changed: Password changed, and your other devices were signed out.

glass.label: Glass intensity
glass.hint: Translucency and blur of the floating chrome only; content stays solid.

display.local_only: Saved on this device only; the hub could not store the preference.

reasoning.label: Show the agent's reasoning
reasoning.hint: A "thought for …" line above the reply, with the text behind a disclosure.

theme.intro: Theme and background of this device. The footer chip changes the same preference.
theme.reduced_note: If your system asks for reduced transparency or motion, the app honours it automatically.

devices.pair_intro: Pair a phone: scan the QR with the Core Hub app, or type the code. The code expires in five minutes.
devices.pairing_expired: The pairing expired. Start a new one.

placeholder.later: {name} arrives with its module in phase {phase}. Nothing is hidden here.

providers.hint: The providers you added. A shared one is added once and every profile uses it; a profile's own is used only in that profile, instead of a shared one of the same kind.
providers.empty: No provider of this kind is configured.
providers.none: No providers yet. Add the first one and its models arrive with it.

provider.key_stored: [stored] — paste a new key to replace it
provider.label: Name
provider.confirm_remove_body: Its key and its model list go with it, and there is no undo.

defaults.hint: This profile's chat and coding models. Every agent here inherits them unless it is pinned to something else; a choice this profile has not made comes from the default profile.
defaults.no_models: No models yet. Add a provider key and the hub fetches its model list.
defaults.inheriting_hint: What each agent will use when a chat does not name a model.

ensembles.hint: Ensembles are created over the API for now; this tab lands with the rooms screens.

test.http_error: The provider answered with an error.

panel.no_models: No models yet. Refresh the model list first.
panel.visibility_all_hint: Including whatever the provider adds later.
panel.visibility_include_hint: Pick them in the table below.
panel.caption: Models of {provider}

add.fetch_failed: The provider did not return a model list.
add.fetch_empty: The provider answered, but listed no models.
add.loopback: This address is loopback, and the hub runs in a container — it would reach the container itself, not your machine. Try {url}, and on a Linux host add extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"] to the stack.
add.scope_all_hint: Shared: every profile uses it, including profiles made later.
add.scope_profile_hint: Only {profile} uses it, and its key wins there over a shared provider of the same kind. Other profiles never see it.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.hint: What the agent runtime received from this profile.

runtime_writable.ok: The hub manages the agent runtime.
runtime_writable.missing: No agent runtime this hub can configure.

provider_keys.ok: Provider keys are in the runtime's environment.
provider_keys.missing: A provider key has not reached the runtime.

provider_verified.ok: Every provider answered its last check.
provider_verified.missing: A provider refused its last check — open it and fix the key.

model_selected.ok: A chat model is selected for the runtime.
model_selected.missing: No chat model is selected — choose one under Defaults.

gateway_reloaded.ok: The runtime restarted after the last change.
gateway_reloaded.missing: The runtime has not restarted since the last change.

working_dir.label: Working folder
working_dir.hint: Where this chat works on disk.
working_dir.automatic_note: the hub names it after the session
working_dir.locked: The folder is fixed once the chat has run.

combobox.error: The list could not be fetched.

queue.title: Message queue
queue.steer_hint: Stop the live turn and take this instead, in the same context.

tasks.no_projects_body: Tasks live inside a project. Create one to start.
tasks.intake_hint: A task arrives here, is specified, and then joins the queue.

hermes.owns_text: This card is on Hermes's board, and this hub does not run Hermes here, so its title and description are Hermes's to change.
hermes.owns_card: This card is on Hermes's board, and this hub does not run Hermes here, so Hermes decides what happens to it.
hermes.writes_through: This card is on Hermes's board: changes are made on Hermes first.
hermes.api_unavailable: Hermes's API is not available right now, so nothing was changed: {message}
hermes.confirm_delete_body: It is deleted from Hermes's board too. This cannot be undone.

assign.title: Assign to an agent
assign.instructions_hint: Optional. Sent to the agent with the task.
assign.no_agents: No agent on this hub can take a task yet. Install or enable one in Agents.
assign.not_started: Handed to this agent's own board: it starts the task from there, not the hub.

handover.title: Hand to another profile
handover.hint: Hermes gives the card to that profile's Hermes, and the card moves to that profile.
handover.no_workspaces: There is no other profile to hand it to.
handover.confirm_running_body: Hermes stops its current run first, then hands the card over.

schedules.new_hint: Saved with its next run computed. A schedule for Hermes runs in Hermes's own scheduler; any other is run by the hub itself.
schedules.name: Name
schedules.prompt: What should the agent be asked?
schedules.cron_hint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday.

hermes.unreachable: Hermes is not answering right now, so nothing was changed.
hermes.timezone: Hermes runs every cron in {zone}. Use that zone, or change Hermes's timezone.
hermes.delivery: Hermes posts to messaging platforms itself — ask for it in the prompt.
hermes.prompt_required: A schedule for Hermes needs a prompt.
hermes.fired: Hermes will run it on its next tick.
hermes.run_options: Hermes decides these two for its own jobs, so they are not set here.

schedules.in_profile: New schedules are made in {name}. To make one in another profile, switch the profile at the top of the page.

options.title: Run options
options.missed_hint: If the hub was not running at its time, it runs once when the hub is back within 24 hours. Unchecked, it never runs late, and the history says so. Up to two minutes late still counts as on time.
options.overlap: If the previous run is still going
options.overlap_hint: "Run now" always starts at once and stops nothing.

skip.label: Skip
skip.hint: This time does not run, and the history says so.

wait.label: Wait, then run
wait.hint: Runs as soon as the previous run ends. Only one time waits; any later one is skipped and recorded.

parallel.label: Run alongside
parallel.hint: Runs in a new conversation next to the previous one.

replace.label: Stop the previous
replace.hint: Stops the previous run for real, then starts.

history.waiting: Waiting for the previous run to end

run.title: Workflow run
run.waiting: This run is waiting for your approval.

notify.none_body: What happens in the hub appears here: a reply that finished, or an approval waiting for you.
notify.quiet_hint: A window in which no notification is pushed to your devices.
notify.push_note: Quiet hours are about device notifications, not the inbox — what is written at night is still here in the morning. Device notifications are not built yet.

webhooks.intro: Addresses this hub calls on its own, signed so the receiver can check the sender. Webhooks belong to the profile you are in.
webhooks.forwarding_note: Today the hub sends a webhook only the test delivery from this page. Forwarding the events you choose is not built yet: they are saved and will be used once it is.
webhooks.none_body: Add one to give an outside service an address the hub can call.
webhooks.no_deliveries: Nothing has been sent to this webhook yet.
webhooks.delete_body: The hub stops calling this address and forgets its delivery history.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.url_hint: An http or https URL. The hub checks where it points before saving it.
webhooks.url_scheme: Use an address that starts with http:// or https://.
webhooks.url_unresolvable: The hub could not find this address. Check the host name.
webhooks.url_private: This address points inside a private network. Allow private addresses below if that is on purpose.
webhooks.allow_private_hint: Off by default, so a webhook cannot make the hub call machines inside its own network.
webhooks.signing_hint: With a secret, every delivery carries the header below, an HMAC-SHA256 of the body, so the receiver can check it came from this hub.
webhooks.secret_new_hint: Shown once after saving; the receiver must be given the new one.
webhooks.secret_make: Sign deliveries with a new secret
webhooks.events_hint: Which of the hub's events this webhook is for. Saved now; sent once forwarding exists.
webhooks.secret_once: Copy it now. The hub keeps it but will never show it again.

privacy.access_hint: Paired phones and integrations each hold a token that acts as you. Revoke one and it stops working at once; a paired device is unlinked.
privacy.revoke_body: Anything using this token loses access at once. This cannot be undone.
privacy.revoke_device_body: This device loses access at once and is unlinked; pairing it again gives it a new token.
privacy.none: No app or device holds a token
privacy.none_body: Only your own sign-ins can reach your account.
privacy.browsers_note: Browsers you signed in to are not listed here. Changing your password under Account signs out every browser except this one; it does not revoke the tokens above.

people.title: People
people.owner_note: The owner account is not edited here
people.password_note: Typed once and never shown again. It ends this person's sessions on every device.
people.delete_body: The account, its tokens and its paired devices go. Conversations stay.
people.username_bad: Two to forty lowercase letters, digits, and . _ -
people.member_can: Opens chats and agents in their profiles
people.admin_can: Manages people, profiles and hub settings
people.no_lockouts_body: An address locks after repeated failed sign-ins and unlocks itself when the time is up.
people.workspaces_hint: A member sees only the profiles chosen here: their chats, agents and tasks.

workspaces.note: Separate profiles: their agents, models and conversations do not see each other.
workspaces.archive_body: The profile is folded away here and its memberships end. Its Hermes profile and its conversations ({sessions}) stay and are not erased.
workspaces.name: Name
workspaces.slug_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes — it appears in links.
workspaces.slug_bad: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with one
workspaces.clone_what: Copies the config, the personality (SOUL.md) and the skills — not memory, chats or channels.
workspaces.origin_blank_what: A fresh Hermes profile with its default settings and bundled skills.
workspaces.rename_hint: Any name, in any language. It is shown wherever this profile appears, and Hermes shows it too. The id {slug} does not change, so chats, channels and schedules keep working.
workspaces.export_what: Hermes writes this profile as its own archive (.tar.gz): its personality (SOUL.md), memory, skills, settings and chats. The file can be imported here, into Ekko, or with hermes profile import.
workspaces.export_secrets: Keys stay behind: credential files (.env, auth.json) are left out, and any provider key stored in this hub is blanked wherever it appears. Only you can download the archive, for 24 hours.
workspaces.import_what: Choose a Hermes profile archive (.tar.gz) — one exported here, from Ekko, or with hermes profile export. Hermes makes a new profile from it under the slug below.
workspaces.import_too_large: The archive is larger than the hub accepts for an upload (50 MB).
workspaces.export_keys_warning: The file will contain this profile's providers with their API keys in the clear — its own and the shared ones it uses. Anyone who has the file can use those keys. Importing it makes them the new profile's own.
workspaces.export_providers_carried: Providers in the file, keys included: {count}

knowledge.more: There is more — narrow the search or the kind.
knowledge.empty_body: Journal entries, notes and files appear here as they are written or attached in a conversation.
knowledge.no_match_body: Change the word, or widen the kind.

plugins.none_body: This hub answers the list and has no installer yet. When one exists, what is installed shows here with its state.
plugins.name: Plugin

updates.web_note: This page is about the phone and desktop apps. The web you are looking at is served by the hub and changes when it does.
updates.from_source_hint: The hub reads GitHub releases itself instead of you uploading them.
updates.token_hint: For a private repository. Written once, never shown.
updates.token_stored: Stored. Type a new one to replace it.
updates.auto_publish: Publish to the test channel automatically
updates.auto_publish_hint: Every new release at the source is published to test on its own.
updates.empty_body: What is published here is what the phone and desktop apps find. None of them is built yet.
updates.delete_body: It disappears from the update list. A build already downloaded keeps working.

about.name: Name
about.realtime_note: What a client opens so it learns what happens without asking.

skills.none_body: Skills are files in the agent's folder. Add one here, or install a pack.
skills.delete_body: The whole skill folder goes, with every file in it. Turning it off keeps everything.
skills.editor_note: This is what the agent reads, verbatim — front matter and body. Nothing is reshaped on save.

reason.pack_unrecognised: A skill pack is a SKILL.md file or a zip archive
reason.pack_path_unsafe: The archive has a path that would land outside its skill
reason.pack_unsupported: The archive uses something the hub does not read
reason.pack_too_large: The archive is too large once unpacked
reason.skill_too_large: SKILL.md is longer than Hermes reads
reason.skill_front_matter_missing: SKILL.md does not start with a front matter block (---)
reason.skill_front_matter_unclosed: SKILL.md's front matter is not closed with ---
reason.skill_front_matter_invalid: SKILL.md's front matter is not valid YAML
reason.skill_name_required: SKILL.md's front matter has no name
reason.skill_description_required: SKILL.md's front matter has no description
reason.skill_description_too_long: The description is longer than Hermes reads
reason.skill_body_empty: SKILL.md has nothing after its front matter
reason.skill_name_invalid: The skill name is not one Hermes accepts
reason.skill_nested: A skill in the archive sits inside another skill
reason.skill_duplicate: The same skill ({skill}) is in the upload twice
reason.skill_exists: This profile already has the skill {skill}; delete it first to replace it

skills.builtin_hint: One of Hermes's own skills. Hermes keeps it in step with its bundle, so it can be read and pinned here but not edited, switched off or deleted.
skills.bundled_refused: This is one of Hermes's own skills; it is read-only here.

mcp.name: Name
mcp.none_body: MCP servers give the agent tools beyond its own. Add one here.
mcp.restart_note: This page writes to the agent's config file. Hermes connects to these servers when it starts, so restart it for a change to take effect.
mcp.editor_note: Every MCP server has its own fields. It is edited as it is, and nothing we do not recognise is dropped. A credential reads as [stored]; leaving it keeps the one on file.
mcp.delete_body: It goes from the config file. Nothing is removed from the server itself.

memory.note: Three documents the agent reads when a conversation starts, so a change here reaches its next conversation. They are emptied by editing, never deleted.
memory.about_soul: Who the agent is. Read at the start of every conversation.
memory.about_memory: What it learned and chose to keep.
memory.empty_soul: Not written yet — the agent has no particular character.
memory.empty_user: It has written nothing about you yet.
memory.entries_hint: A list of short entries, each separated by a line holding only §. It has a character limit: past it, the agent cannot add anything new.
memory.too_long: Too long for this memory: {length} characters, and the limit is {limit}. Shorten or merge entries.

channels.none_body: Channels are added in the agent's config file. Whatever is in it appears here.
channels.restart_note: This page writes to the agent's config file. Hermes connects to these platforms when it starts, so restart it for a change to take effect.
channels.editor_note: The fields come from the agent's file, not from a form we wrote. A secret reads as [stored]; leaving it keeps the one on file.
channels.secret_hint: Leave it to keep the one already stored.
channels.no_fields: This channel has no fields yet.
channels.clear_body: The tokens and secrets are removed and the channel is switched off. Its other settings stay.

login.title: Link {name}
login.note: Hermes pairs this profile's agent with a phone. Scan the code from WhatsApp on the phone: Settings → Linked devices → Link a device.
login.done: Linked. The agent answers on it after its next restart.
login.done_as: Linked as {account}. The agent answers on it after its next restart.
login.not_supported: This platform does not pair by QR; fill in its fields instead.
login.done_now: Linked. The agent answers on it now; the first person to message it waits for your approval here.
login.done_as_now: Linked as {account}. The agent answers on it now; the first person to message it waits for your approval here.

channels.unlink_body: The agent stops answering this number, its session is deleted from this profile and the channel is switched off. Approved senders stay. Remove the device on the phone too: WhatsApp → Linked devices.
channels.unlinked_note: Unlinked. Remove the device from WhatsApp on the phone too: Settings → Linked devices.
channels.unlink_not_linked: No number is linked in this profile.
channels.unlink_not_supported: This platform is not linked to a device, so there is nothing to unlink; forget its identity instead.
channels.applies_now: In this profile the hub restarts the messaging gateway itself, so a change takes effect at once.

how.title: How to use it
how.step_message: 1) Message the linked number from another WhatsApp account.
how.step_approve: 2) The sender receives a pairing code and the request appears here under “Waiting for approval”: approve it and the agent starts answering them.
how.step_restart: In the default profile, restart Hermes from its card first so it starts answering.
how.personal_warning: Warning: if you link your personal number, everyone who messages it receives the agent's pairing reply. A number dedicated to the agent is better.

pairing.title: Waiting for approval
pairing.note: Someone who messages the agent for the first time receives a pairing code and waits here. A request expires after an hour. The list refreshes every ten seconds.
pairing.revoke_body: The agent will not answer them any more, and their next message becomes a new pairing request.

telegram.title: Link Telegram
telegram.intro: The agent answers on a Telegram bot of your own. You make the bot in Telegram in a minute; the hub never makes one for you.
telegram.step_open: Open Telegram and search for @BotFather (the official one, with the blue tick).
telegram.step_newbot: Send /newbot, then choose a name and a username ending in “bot”.
telegram.step_copy: BotFather replies with a token like 123456789:AA… — copy it and paste it below.
telegram.token_hint: Kept as a secret in this profile's Hermes files and never shown again.
telegram.allowed_hint: Telegram user IDs, separated by commas. To find yours, message @userinfobot in Telegram. Everyone else gets a pairing code to approve here.
telegram.allowed_invalid: A Telegram user ID is digits only.
telegram.done_now: The agent answers on the bot now. The first person to message it waits for your approval below.
telegram.done_restart: In the default profile, restart Hermes from its card so it starts answering on the bot.
telegram.token_invalid: That does not look like a bot token. It is the bot's number, a colon, and a long code, as BotFather sent it.
telegram.token_rejected: Telegram refused this token: {message}. Copy it again from BotFather (or /token there for a new one).
telegram.unreachable: Telegram did not answer. Check the hub's internet connection and try again.
telegram.token_in_use: This bot is already linked in the profile “{profile}”. A bot answers in one place only: unlink it there first.
telegram.how_message: 2) Send it any message. It replies with a pairing code.
telegram.how_approve: 3) Approve the request below under “Waiting for approval”; from then on the agent answers.
telegram.unlink_body: The token is removed from this profile and the agent stops answering on the bot. The bot itself stays in Telegram (delete it with @BotFather if you want). The people you allowed stay listed.
telegram.unlinked_note: Unlinked. The bot no longer answers from this profile.

settings.title: Telegram settings
settings.applies_now: Saving restarts this profile's gateway, so changes apply at once.
settings.applies_restart: In the default profile, changes apply after Hermes restarts.
settings.media_note: These are the profile's own settings: they change WhatsApp and every other channel of this profile too.
settings.shared: Also changes WhatsApp and other channels
settings.invalid: This value is not accepted. Check the format.
settings.saved_now: Saved. The gateway restarts with the new settings.
settings.saved_restart: Saved. Restart Hermes from its card for them to apply.

allowed_users.label: People who skip approval
allowed_users.help: Telegram user IDs that may message the bot without a pairing code. Find yours by messaging @userinfobot.

unauthorized_dm_behavior.label: When a stranger messages the bot
unauthorized_dm_behavior.help: Send them a pairing code to approve here, or ignore them silently.

show_reasoning.label: Show the model's thinking
show_reasoning.help: Before each answer, add the model's reasoning as a separate block.

reasoning_style.label: How the thinking looks
reasoning_style.help: The format of the thinking block.

tool_progress.label: Show what the agent is doing
tool_progress.help: Messages about the tools the agent uses while it works.

cleanup_progress.label: Remove progress messages when done
cleanup_progress.help: Delete the “working…” and tool messages after a successful answer.

streaming.label: Write the answer as it comes
streaming.help: Show the answer while it is being written, by editing one message, instead of sending it at the end.

reply_to_mode.label: Reply as a quote
reply_to_mode.help: Whether answers quote the message they answer.

reactions.label: Reactions
reactions.help: React with 👀 while working and ✅ or ❌ when done.

disable_link_previews.label: No link previews
disable_link_previews.help: Send links without Telegram's preview card.

notifications.label: Notification sound
notifications.help: Which bot messages make the phone ring.

require_mention.label: Answer in groups only when mentioned
require_mention.help: In a group, the bot answers only messages that @mention it or reply to it. Private chats are not affected.

allowed_chats.label: Only these groups
allowed_chats.help: Group chat IDs the bot answers in (IDs of groups start with -100). Empty: any group it is added to.

free_response_chats.label: Groups where no mention is needed
free_response_chats.help: Group chat IDs where the bot answers every message even when mentions are required.

group_allowed_users.label: People allowed in groups
group_allowed_users.help: Telegram user IDs whose group messages the bot answers. This does not let them message it privately.

observe_unmentioned_group_messages.label: Read group messages it does not answer
observe_unmentioned_group_messages.help: Keep unmentioned group messages as context for the next answer.

guest_mode.label: Answer a mention in any group
guest_mode.help: Answer an @mention even in groups not in the list above.

exclusive_bot_mentions.label: Ignore messages for other bots
exclusive_bot_mentions.help: Skip a group message that mentions another bot.

allow_bots.label: Messages from other bots
allow_bots.help: Whether messages sent by other bots are answered.

stt_enabled.label: Transcribe voice notes
stt_enabled.help: Voice notes people send are turned into text for the agent.

stt_echo_transcripts.label: Show the transcript
stt_echo_transcripts.help: Send the transcribed text back so the person sees what was understood.

voice_auto_tts.label: Answer with voice notes
voice_auto_tts.help: Answers are also sent as voice. In a chat, /voice changes this for that chat.

home_channel.label: Home chat
home_channel.help: The chat ID where scheduled tasks and notices are delivered. In Telegram, /sethome in a chat sets it too.

gateway_restart_notification.label: Say when back online
gateway_restart_notification.help: Send a message to the home chat when the agent restarts.

command_menu_max.label: Commands in the menu
command_menu_max.help: How many commands the bot's “/” menu lists (1–100).

proxy_url.label: Proxy
proxy_url.help: Reach Telegram through a proxy, e.g. socks5://host:1080. Leave empty for a direct connection.

question.title: Question
question.expired: Time ran out without an answer

agent_jobs.note: What runs on its own for this agent in this profile. For Hermes these are the jobs in its own scheduler, and Hermes runs them. They are the same schedules the Schedules page shows; make or edit one there.
agent_jobs.none_body: Nothing is scheduled for this agent in this profile. Make a schedule on the Schedules page and it shows here.
agent_jobs.delete_body: It is deleted from Hermes's scheduler too.

agent_plugins.note: The plugins Hermes has in this profile, with Hermes's own status. One that is not enabled does not load — except the messaging platforms and model providers Hermes ships, which load when they are used. A change reaches the agent's next session.
agent_plugins.none_body: Hermes lists no plugin in this profile.
agent_plugins.install_hint: A name from Hermes's plugin catalog, owner/repo, or a Git URL. Hermes fetches it, scans it and installs it into this profile switched off; switch it on when you are ready.
agent_plugins.remove_body: Its folder is removed from this profile's plugins. Switching it off keeps it.
agent_plugins.bundled_refused: This plugin ships with Hermes; switch it off instead of removing it.

trajectory.no_details: Nothing more was recorded for this step.
trajectory.empty_body: Send a message and each step the agent takes appears here.
trajectory.untimed: This conversation is from before the hub recorded step times, so there is no timeline — only the steps.
trajectory.partial: Earlier turns were recorded before the hub kept step times; the timeline shows the rest.

files.title: Files
files.empty: No files yet. What the agent writes in this conversation's folder, and what is attached, appears here.
files.truncated: The folder holds more files than are listed; the newest are shown.
files.load_failed: The files could not be read.
files.too_large: This file is too large to show here ({size}). Download it to open it.
files.no_preview: This kind of file cannot be shown here. Download it to open it.
files.columns_capped: Only the first {count} columns are shown.
files.pptx_outline: An outline of the slides' titles and text. The slides themselves are not drawn here; download the file to see them.
files.docx_note: The text of the document; pictures and page layout are not shown.

office_error.too_many_entries: The file holds too many parts to open safely.
office_error.too_large: The file unpacks to more than can be opened safely.
office_error.not_office: This is not the Office file its name says.
office_error.damaged: The file is damaged and cannot be read.

files.html_note: Shown in a sandbox: its scripts run apart from this app and it cannot contact anything.
files.gone: This file is no longer in the conversation's folder.
